connector: Have you ever done something brave while you were scared? This week you read two texts about courage. Text 1 explains what courage is. Watch for what the author says courage is, and what it is not.

a.raw: courage isnt the same as having no fear
a.fixed: Courage isn’t the same as having no fear.
a.why: Courage starts the sentence. Isn’t joins is and not. A period ends it.

b.raw: mira didnt feel brave but she walked onto the bridge
b.fixed: Mira didn’t feel brave, but she walked onto the bridge.
b.why: Mira is a name. Didn’t joins did and not. A comma goes before but.

cards.title: World Notes: Grace Darling, a Real Rescue
cards.sub: A real person and place behind this week's game
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: On September 7, 1838, a steamship called the Forfarshire hit the rocks off the Farne Islands, in England, during a terrible storm. Some of the people on board were left clinging to a rock.
Grace Darling, who was 22, lived in the Longstone Lighthouse with her family. At dawn she saw the people on the rock.
Grace and her father, William, rowed their heavy boat nearly a mile through the waves and saved nine people. This week's game follows their boat.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. This week is all about courage. Text 1 explains what courage is. Read to find out.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: prefixes and suffixes, a year of grammar, and long words.
transcripts.guide2: Read Text 1 with your lens. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you plan your comparison and write your claim.

notes.wordParts: Prefixes and suffixes from this year: re- = again, un- = not, trans- = across, inter- = between, -ful = full of, -less = without.
notes.grammar: Year review: capitals for names and the first word, a comma after an opening part, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, and irregular past forms like went and took.
notes.spelling: Long words: find the vowels, split between them, read each chunk, then push the chunks together. Rescue = res + cue.
notes.wgrd: Text 1 says courage is not having no fear. It is choosing to act anyway, because it matters, one choice at a time.
vocab: having or showing courage; willing to act even when afraid
continuing to try even when things are hard
a quality that shows good character

mods.script: [warmly] Here's this week's reading tip. Two authors can write about the same topic and still say different things about it. This week the topic is courage. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. Bravery isn't the absence of fear; it's choosing to act anyway. Isn't joins is and not. It's joins it and is. The mark in the middle, a semicolon, joins two complete thoughts that belong together. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Think about the questions. Tap See what was hiding. Type the missing part in each box.
mods.script: [curious] What happens when you add a part to a word? Replay. Re is a prefix at the front. It means again. Replay means play again. Painless. Less is a suffix at the end. It means without. Painless means without pain. Every part on this page is one you already know. Read the parts, tap See what was hiding, then type the missing part of each word.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Daring. Here's my sentence. Grace made a daring trip across the stormy sea. One, read the sentence: she went, even though it was dangerous. Two, look for word parts: dare, plus i n g. Three, check it. Daring means brave enough to take a risk. Now fill in each sentence from the word bank, and play the matching game.

A comma goes after wreck, to close the opening part. And telled should be told. Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap all six words in the passage that need fixing.

items.t: Someone tells the truth when it would be easier to lie.

items.why: Text 1 says this takes courage, even though it is not a battle.
